input.question: Why do some people binge eat when they're stressed, while others lose their appetite entirely?
input.ground_truth: I'm gonna call the genetic variation card here. Eating while you're stressed makes sense for many reasons (additional energy may aid in alleviating the cause of the stress, plus the happiness of eating cancels out the unhappiness left by stress). However the inverse also has it's advantages (i.e, if you're in a sticky situation, thinking about eating may not be the most productive thing to do). Psychological factors may also be at play, including strength of will and how the specific person perceives eating.

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have two friends, Sam and Alex.

When Sam feels really stressed—maybe because he had a bad day at school or is worried about something—his body tells him, "Give me food!" So Sam eats a lot of snacks all at once. This is called binge eating. It's like when you really want your favorite ice cream and you eat it all up quickly because you want to feel better.

But Alex, when he feels stressed, doesn't want any food at all. His body says, "No thanks, I'm not hungry!" So he might not eat anything, even if he's supposed to have lunch or dinner. This is called losing your appetite.

Why does this happen? Well, when people feel stressed, their bodies can react in different ways. Some people's bodies want comfort food to feel better, so they eat more. Other people's bodies get so nervous or upset that they don't feel like eating at all.

It's like how some people hug a teddy bear when they're sad, and some people just want to be alone and quiet. Everyone is a little different!
